title: Questlove - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 148,234. Ahmir Khalib Thompson, born 20 January 1971, Philadelphia; father Arthur Lee Andrews Thompson (Lee Andrews of Lee Andrews & the Hearts), mother Jacquelin Thompson (Congress Alley); toured with his parents, worked the lights at 10, at 12 drummed for his father's band at Radio City Music Hall; Philadelphia High School for the Creative and Performing Arts (classmates Boyz II Men, Christian McBride, Joey DeFrancesco); jazz and composition classes at the Settlement Music School after; co-founded the Square Roots with Tariq Trotter; Organix (1993) credited to 'B.R.O. the R.?'; the name from A Tribe Called Quest; Soulquarians; executive producer of D'Angelo's Voodoo (2000), Common's Like Water for Chocolate and Electric Circus, Mos Def's Black on Both Sides; drums or production on Erykah Badu's Baduizm and Mama's Gun; The Philadelphia Experiment (2001, with Christian McBride and Uri Caine); house band of Late Night with Jimmy Fallon from 2 March 2009 and of The Tonight Show from 2014; Mo' Meta Blues (2013, with Ben Greenman); Summer of Soul (2021): Sundance Grand Jury Prize and Audience Award, the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature (2022), the BAFTA; six Grammys (including 'You Got Me', 2000, and The Road from Memphis with Booker T., 2012).

title: The Roots - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 180,298. Formed in Philadelphia in 1987 by Questlove and Black Thought, students at CAPA; Organix (1993, independent, London); Do You Want More?!!!??! (1995, DGC); Illadelph Halflife (1996); Things Fall Apart (1999; No. 4, platinum); The Roots Come Alive (1999, live); Phrenology (2002, MCA, gold); The Tipping Point (2004, No. 4); Game Theory (2006, Def Jam); Rising Down (2008); How I Got Over (2010); Undun (2011, Def Jam); Dave Chappelle's Block Party (2006), the film of a September 2004 show; house band for Late Night from March 2009 and The Tonight Show from February 2014.

title: Questlove, Red Bull Music Academy lecture, New York, 2013 (with Jeff 'Chairman' Mao; transcript)
notes: Read through a summariser that capped quotes at 125 characters, so the quotes are short. 'My idol was a drummer named Steve Ferrone, from a band called The Average White Band'; Ferrone 'was actually from the Bernard Purdie school of drumming'; 'James Gadson is one of my earlier drumming heroes, he used to drum for Bill Withers in the '70s'; 'there's cats like Chris Dave that have me losing sleep'; 'my father's dream was for me to be a session drummer'; drumming for his father 'from like 13 'till about 20-something'; 'Keep it in the pocket'; 'I clocked in my 10,000 hours as a kid, practicing'; on Illadelph Halflife, 'I wanted to be the coldest, most emotionless, just an absolute machine'; Dilla 'programmed his drums with no quantize'; the Pharcyde kick 'sounded like the kick drum was played by like a drunk three-year-old'; 'this whole drunken-style-but-staying-on-beat thing'; D'Angelo 'wanted me to drag the beat, but then he'd drag the beat behind me', 'I want you to do it drunker than that'; 'most of my Voodoo stuff was just rimshot funk, not hitting the snare at all'; 'I did every conceivable experiment until I felt my drums were dirty and cold'; a blanket over the snare; 'I would use a click track sometimes ... half sampling myself, half using click tracks'. No Al Jackson, Stubblefield, Starks, Tony Allen or Zigaboo in the transcript.

title: J-Zone, 'Give The Drummer Some: Questlove', Red Bull Music Academy Daily, 6 February 2019
notes: Read through a summariser (quotes capped at 125 characters). 'Breakbeat drumming is just taking all the elements away, and keeping it meat and potatoes'; he represents 'those drummers that you won't hear about in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame': Purdie and Steve Ferrone, 'and of course Stubblefield and Starks, but there's just a whole slew of cats from these independent mom-and-pop labels'; James Gadson drummed on D'Angelo's 'Sugah Daddy'; on Al Green's Lay It Down: 'for me I morphed into Al Jackson, like I lowered the shit out of my snare', 'Howard Grimes, yeah, and Al Jackson'; Dilla: 'It sounded like a drunk three year old programmed this kick drum'; Voodoo: 'Before, I was just playing without a click, but now I gotta program myself'; Black Messiah: 'I gotta do the exact opposite of what I did on Voodoo', 'where I had a lot of fun not being me'; The Charade with the snare wires off and the drums tuned low; Joe Tarsia: tape the drums, 'Stop playing so damn hard'; a new drum set in December 1978; joined his father's band at 12 when the drummer broke his arm.

title: Jason King, 'How the Video for "Untitled" Might Have Ruined D'Angelo's Career', Slate, 15 February 2013
notes: King's interviews for the Voodoo story. Questlove: 'Dilla would program his drums non-quantized: in layman's speak, it's the equivalent of having a 5-year old play drums'; D'Angelo 'wanted me to play as drunk and as slow and as dusted as I've ever played in my life'; 'I need you to keep the pocket but don't drag behind me, but play a little crooked'; 'I was just a kind of super-metronome; I spent three years of trying to hide myself'; 'strip yourself of all that coldness and play human'; studying old tapes and Soul Train episodes at Electric Lady before working on a song.

title: Voodoo (D'Angelo album) - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 211,053. Released 25 January 2000 (Virgin, Cheeba Sound); recorded 1998-1999 at Electric Lady Studios, from sessions begun in 1996; produced by D'Angelo, DJ Premier and Raphael Saadiq; Russell Elevado on analog tape; most tracks live with no instrument overdubs, 'Untitled (How Does It Feel)' the exception; Questlove on drums, co-writer of four songs, D'Angelo's 'co-pilot'; grooves set back on the beat; double rimshots behind the beat on 'Greatdayndamornin' / Booty'; 'One Mo'Gin' a rocksteady rhythm; J Dilla uncredited but an influence on the rhythm; D'Angelo sequenced the bass lines for Pino Palladino; Steve McPherson: the timing 'can't be measured in beats or fractions of beats in a meaningful way'; the Voodoo tour from 1 March 2000 (House of Blues, Los Angeles), nearly eight months, with the Soultronics, assembled and directed by Questlove.

title: Things Fall Apart (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 23 February 1999, MCA; recorded 1997-1998 at Electric Lady and the Cutting Room, New York; produced mainly by the Grand Wizzards with James Poyser, J Dilla, Kamal Gray, Questlove, Scott Storch and others; sessions overlapping Brown Sugar, Baduizm and Common's One Day It'll All Make Sense, about 145 songs narrowed to 14; 'You Got Me' (22 January 1999) won the 2000 Grammy for Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group; 'The Next Movement'; gold April 1999, platinum April 2013, No. 4 on the Billboard 200.

title: Like Water for Chocolate (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Common, released 28 March 2000, MCA; Electric Lady Studios and Studio A, Dearborn Heights; Questlove executive producer; production mostly J Dilla, with James Poyser, DJ Premier, D'Angelo and Karriem Riggins; Questlove drums on 'Cold Blooded', 'Geto Heaven Part Two' and 'A Song for Assata'; Karriem Riggins drums on track 16.

title: Lay It Down (Al Green album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 27 May 2008, Blue Note; produced by Questlove and James Poyser; Questlove drums on tracks 1-10, Homer Steinweiss on 11; Adam Blackstone bass, the Dap-Kings Horns, Larry Gold's strings; two Grammys at the 51st awards ('Stay with Me (By the Sea)', 'You've Got the Love I Need'), nominated for Best R&B Album.

title: 'Hip-Hop House Band: ?uestlove and the Roots', Yamaha All Access, issue 20 (c. 2010)
notes: Read in full (PDF). Undated; it names How I Got Over as 'the new Roots album' (2010). A 1967 Yamaha kit on the Fallon show, 'one of the first Yamaha drum sets ever made'; several Yamaha snares, his favourite the David Garibaldi signature 'because I get such a great snap out of it'; 'I like a dead, vintage sound, not too refined'; Beech Customs 'help me get an old, raggedy sound, as opposed to a polished one'; 'I consider myself more of an engineer than a musician or producer'; 'We knew we didn't want to sample, but we wanted to have the same gritty quality you get from sample-based hip-hop. I'd drum for an hour with one mic combo, then another'; 'I was the guinea pig for the SubKick. They made it for me back during the D'Angelo tour in 2000'; 'dirty, gritty, and raw - real gutbucket funk'; 'the more I listen to '70s stuff, the more I realize that the drums just aren't that loud'; How I Got Over tracked on his show kit in the dressing room; 'just yesterday I had the pleasure of playing with one of my drumming idols: Tony Allen, Fela Kuti's drummer'. The photographs show his afro and full beard, and a kit with a Yamaha bass drum head.

title: John Lingan, Backbeats: A History of Rock and Roll in Fifteen Drummers (2025), excerpt in Philadelphia Magazine, 14 November 2025
notes: The Questlove chapter, excerpted. 'His job was to reverse-engineer a sampler, to play like a machine that was made to replicate a human timekeeper'; on Distortion to Static (1995): 'You wouldn't know that Questlove's kit has any toms at all. His snare cracks without any vibrations, and his bass drum is tuned low enough to feel speaker-bumping'; 'The game was repetition, not improvisation'; Phrenology 'the Roots' masterpiece', 'Questlove's drums boom like Led Zeppelin's John Bonham busting out of a broken boom box'; his father took him to hear Bernard Purdie explain 'how he keeps food on the table': 'The two and the four'; Dilla's off-grid placement carried into Things Fall Apart and Voodoo.

title: Questlove's Gear - Equipboard
notes: Fan-compiled, each item with its evidence. A 1976 Ludwig Cream Vistalite kit, his own words 'I only used this 76 Ludwig Cream/Vistalites on this record' (the record unnamed); Ludwig Breakbeats on Undun; a Yamaha Maple Custom Absolute (22x18 bass drum, 14x3.5 brass and 14x5.5 snares, 10 and 12 toms, 16 and 18 floor toms; from DrummerWorld, undated); Zildjian 24-inch K Light ride, 20-inch FX Oriental 'Crash of Doom', 14-inch K Constantinople and A Quick Beat hats; Remo Ambassador heads; Vic Firth signature stick, 'as light as I could design it', often held with mainly three fingers; a Big Fat Snare Drum mute; a Yamaha SubKick (c. 2015 photo).

title: Ludwig LC179XX Breakbeats by Questlove 4-piece shell kit (retailer listing, zZounds)

title: Anne Danielsen, 'Shaping the Beat Bin in Computer-Based Grooves', in Performing Time: Synchrony and Temporal Flow in Music and Dance, ed. Clemens Wöllner and Justin London (Oxford University Press, 2023)
notes: On D'Angelo's 'Left & Right' (Voodoo): the drum kit and bass entering introduce 'a discrepancy between the two pulse-carrying layers of around 50 (beats 1 and 3) to 80 (beats 2 and 4) ms', 'between 8% and 12% of a quarter note at the song's tempo of 92 beats per minute'. Which layer is early is not said in the part read. Builds on her 'Here, there and everywhere: three accounts of pulse in D'Angelo's "Left and Right"', in Musical Rhythm in the Age of Digital Reproduction (Ashgate, 2010), which was not read.

title: Neo soul - Wikipedia
notes: Read to character 100,000 of 110,488. A soul revival of the 1980s and 1990s; the term coined by Kedar Massenburg in the late 1990s, largely after D'Angelo's Brown Sugar (1995); from soul, R&B, hip-hop, quiet storm, funk and jazz; D'Angelo, Erykah Badu, Maxwell, Lauryn Hill; the Soulquarians (D'Angelo, the Roots, Badu, Bilal, Mos Def, Common, James Poyser, J Dilla, Q-Tip), Questlove driving much of their production; live instruments over sampling; Danielsen on grooves manipulated at the microrhythmic level in the late 1990s.
